owner_directive: Rowan, 2026-11-14: all calls are recorded and monitored. Every recording, dictation and chat is fed into audits and back-end processes: the content is the request, the meta content (sentiment, frustration, repetition, corrections, ideas, stalls) feeds process improvement and the code loop. Wherever the product captures the microphone or voice-to-text, that capture is monitored for issues and roadmap items too: what it means for the whole system, not only the words.
rule: Every owner utterance (typed, dictated, transcribed audio) is a signal, and every microphone interaction is a telemetry event. The server records them, extracts meta signals with a deterministic detector (no model call, no cost), and files each kind as a roadmap issue with owner, trigger and probe. A client never summarizes or files these by hand.
consent: Capture applies to the owner's own sessions and to tenants who opted in at the consent screen; raw audio is never stored, only transcript text, mic event codes and extracted signals. Suppression and opt-out are honored first.

patterns: \bi'?m not going to keep telling you\b
detectors.roadmap: Find the root cause of the repeated failure and remove it in code; add a probe.
A directive was stated more than once: encode it as a doctrine rule with a lint, not a memory.
The agent misread the request: add the ambiguity to the interview questions or the glossary.
Queue as an idea in the intake lane for the product manager role.
A surface or message was unclear: simplify the copy or the step (zero-fuss principle).
A loop is slower than the owner's patience: measure its latency and add an SLA.
Record what worked; protect it with a test so it is not regressed.

The owner found a problem before the system did (OWNER-FIRST-1). Add the missing detector to doctrine/detectors.json, add a row to ops/owner-reports.jsonl naming it, and fix the problem; `python3 -m foundation selftest --owner` fails until every report names a live detector.

mic_events.doc: Emitted by the voice surfaces (site/interview.js mic button, and any future capture). Event codes only, no audio. A code is a signal once it crosses its threshold within the window.

not-allowed.roadmap: Microphone blocked: show a one-tap fix and the typing fallback earlier; measure permission grant rate.

service-not-allowed.roadmap: Speech service refused: add the on-device fallback (Vosk) so dictation works without the browser service.

no-speech.roadmap: Dictation heard nothing: tune the prompt and silence timeout; check the device input level hint.

network.roadmap: Browser speech needs network and failed: on-device recognition fallback.

audio-capture.roadmap: No usable microphone: surface typing first for this device class.

unsupported.roadmap: Browser has no speech recognition: count the share and decide on a hosted transcription path.

busy.roadmap: Recognition could not start: debounce and recover automatically.

edited-after-dictation.roadmap: Owner corrected the dictated text: collect before/after pairs to tune vocabulary and the glossary.

abandoned.roadmap: Owner pressed the mic then left with no submit: this step loses people, simplify it.

ingest: POST /api/meta/ingest on the site Worker (JSON: source, text or code, at); stored in KV as meta:<iso>:<rand>; the tick Worker drains it through the same detectors into the sink and files META-<n> issues.
